title: File BL-29: nothing makes an unattended run confirm its budget before it spends
body:
One entry appended to `docs/BACKLOG.md`. No code.

**What it records.** The owner ruled on 2026-08-24 (in `docs/DECISIONS.md`) that before every unattended run the agent asks which limit governs the run and what value to use — and prefers that confirmation even where a default exists. The ruling arrived inside **BL-24**, whose subject is where a usage reading comes from, and was recorded there and nowhere else.

So it currently lives as one sentence inside a decision about something else. Nothing enforces it, and nothing carries it to the next project — and it says nothing about this pipeline. It is a rule about how an agent behaves before spending someone's subscription, which is true of every project the template produces.

**Proposed home: `AGENTS.md`, and therefore the template.** `AGENTS.md` here is template-synced, so a rule written only into this repository's copy is lost at the next sync or survives only here. That is the same failure the escapes ledger keeps recording: a fix applied to an instance while the generator stays unchanged buys exactly one instance.

**Filed here rather than as an escape, deliberately.** An escape row answers "what went wrong that a gate should have caught". Nothing has gone wrong — Stage B has not run, no budget has been spent unattended, and there is no incident. Filing it as an escape would put an event in an incident log that never happened. If an unattended run ever does spend without confirming, THAT is the escape, and this item is what it will cite.

The owner was offered the escape route and the direct-to-template route and chose this one.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh`, `backlog-append-only.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
